claim.statement: On 27 April 2026, NourNews quoted Food and Drug Organization head Mehdi Pirsalehi saying Iran's 1405 preferential FX budget gives medicine and pharmaceutical raw materials $1.5 billion inside a $3 billion food/drug allocation, but projected medicine and raw-material import need is about $2.2 billion and the drug office can cover at most half the need from $1.1 billion net preferential FX; he also said 65% of medicine/equipment debt had been paid by the end of 1404 and about $400 million of 1405 resources would go to past clearance settlements.
claim.subject: Iran's medicine and pharmaceutical raw-material supply
claim.object: a preferential-FX shortfall and old-debt draw on 1405 resources

evidence.summary: NourNews reports the FDA head's figures: $1.5B medicine/raw-material preferential allocation, $2.2B projected need, $1.1B net preferential FX covering at most half, 65% debt paid, and $400M earmarked for old clearance settlements.
Existing KNB source records the FDA's earlier warning that damaged firms, FX need, insurance budget limits, and price correction pressure threatened industry continuity.
Existing KNB source records the Health Commission warning that late FX allocation can put patients into a drug crisis.

information_depth.rationale: The source gives named official budget figures and aligns with earlier FDA/parliamentary warnings already in KNB.

claim.statement: On 23-24 April 2026, domestic reporting showed medicine-price relief was selective and operationally incomplete: KhabarOnline/Mahr said about 5,000 drug items had been repriced but basic insurers had not clearly answered whether all were covered and FDA head Mehdi Pirsalehi said resource uncertainty meant new prices were not fully applied in systems, while Mehr reported Social Security copay exemption only for hemophilia, thalassemia, and dialysis drugs inside base-insurer commitment lists, with the special/hard-to-treat fund paying only part of other costs.
claim.subject: Iranian medicine insurance coverage after repricing
claim.object: opaque, incomplete in systems, and selective by patient category

evidence.summary: KhabarOnline/Mahr reports about 5,000 repriced medicines, unclear base-insurer coverage, and Pirsalehi saying resource uncertainty prevented full system application.
Mehr reports Social Security's narrow copay exemption for hemophilia, thalassemia, and dialysis drugs inside base-insurer commitment lists.
Existing KNB source records the Rare Diseases Foundation warning that unclear patient definitions can exclude rare-disease patients from support.
Existing KNB source records earlier parliamentary acknowledgement that coordination failures raised some patient payment shares.

information_depth.rationale: Multiple domestic official-facing reports describe the same administrative problem from pricing, insurance, and patient-category angles.

claim.statement: A 1-2 May 2026 Persian xPool medicine query completed 10 pages and emitted 36 items; it kept medicine scarcity visible through a Baluchistan insulin-price/shortage post, a Shiraz pharmacy-worker-style scarcity list, and broad shortage/food-insecurity complaints, but did not surface a clean in-country patient protest or association-coordination cluster after 1 May.
claim.subject: Persian X medicine-access discourse
claim.object: a clean patient protest or association-coordination cluster

evidence.summary: The final xPool result emitted 36 items after 10 pages and contained medicine-scarcity chatter but no clean patient protest cluster.
The notes summarize the manual read and distinguish household medicine access from prison/rights medicine-denial items.
The earlier v16 xPool source already showed a low-confidence medicine/insulin scarcity social cluster, so v32 updates visibility rather than proving a new mobilization wave.

information_depth.rationale: The job completed, but X discourse is noisy and social visibility cannot prove the absence of local patient action.

assessment.uncertainty: Needs patient-association statements, hospital/pharmacy queue reporting, insurer reimbursement data, or local protest footage after May 1.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v32 - medicine crisis is becoming budget and insurance rationing
synthesis.summary: The thirty-second pass refreshes health access after the earlier medicine/insulin rows. It does not overturn the v16 read; it hardens it. Patient-side reports had already shown insulin scarcity, drug price jumps, rare-disease coverage uncertainty, and treatment triage by workers and retirees. The new delta is official mechanics: the Food and Drug Organization now says preferential FX can cover at most about half the medicine and pharmaceutical raw-material need, while part of 1405 resources is already needed for past clearance settlements. KhabarOnline/Mahr says about 5,000 drug items were repriced, base-insurer coverage remains unclear, and resource uncertainty prevented full system application. Social Security's announced relief is narrow, exempting hemophilia, thalassemia, and dialysis patients only for drugs already inside base-insurer commitment lists, while rare-disease groups still warn that unclear definitions can exclude patients. Fresh xPool chatter keeps medicine scarcity visible but diffuse, with no clean post-May-1 patient protest cluster. Net: the health crack is shifting from anecdotal pharmacy pain into quiet administrative rationing by FX, insurance systems, and patient category; the missing trigger is visible patient or association mobilization.
synthesis.limitations: Official budget and insurance figures show rationing pressure, not actual pharmacy stock levels by city. xPool evidence is noisy and can miss local patient action. The next useful evidence is insurer reimbursement lag data, pharmacy dispensing data by named medicines, hospital treatment deferral, patient-association statements, and any protest or queue footage after May 1.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines direct official budget/insurance reporting, earlier patient-side KNB rows, and a bounded current xPool read.

operations.rationale: A preferential-FX shortfall and old-debt draw are direct indicators for whether price shock becomes measurable drug shortage.
A systemic medicine-financing shortfall is upstream of the mass-mortality question, though mortality requires separate outcome evidence.
Opaque and incomplete insurance updates are exactly the kind of administrative data needed to quantify skipped treatment and medicine access.
Selective coverage and unclear patient categories directly update the rare-disease insurance warning question.
The completed May 1-2 X sample weakly tests whether medicine and insulin grievances are turning into visible patient protest.
Diffuse medicine-cost discourse without coordination updates whether patients, retirees, and workers are converging into shared protest language.

operations.reason: v32 updates the active read from campus restricted reopening to health-access pressure: medicine scarcity and price pain are becoming budget/insurance rationing, while visible patient mobilization remains weak.
